To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) multi-shot re-id is a significantly more challenging task than single-shot re-id; (b) the best re-id performance is achieved by fusing the output of several feature extractors and ranking methods; and (c) the best feature extractors are the ones that incorporate local and global information in a discriminative manner.

(i) the performance of the state of the art in person re-identification (i.e. the performance that is reported by researchers) is 2% higher on VIPeR, CAVIar, and GRID datasets, 3% higher on Market-1501 and DukeMTMC-ReID datasets, 4% higher on CUHK03 and CUHK01 datasets, and 6% higher on iLIDSVID dataset than the performance of the current state of the art

(1) the performance of state-of-the-art algorithms is significantly better than that reported in the literature, (2) the use of multiple features and metric learning algorithms is beneficial, (3) multi-shot re-id performance is significantly better than single-shot re-id performance, (4) the use of a large training set improves re-id performance, and (5) the use of person attributes improves re-id performance
In summary, our research is concerned with
three major aspects of re-id algorithms: 1) features, 2) metrics, and 3) datasets.

the following three aspects: (1) we provide a systematic review of the most recent advances on person re-identification, (2) we propose a unified codebase for re-identification, which is publicly available for the community to use, and (3) we conduct extensive experiments and provide benchmark results for the community

the following contributions: 1) a systematic review and evaluation of state-of-the-art re-id methods, 2) a large-scale re-id dataset with a realistic problem setting, 3) a unified code library for re-id algorithms that includes 11 features and 22 metrics, 4) an extensive evaluation and benchmark that will serve as a baseline for future research, and 5) a new large-scale re-id evaluation dataset.

the state of the art in person re-identification is not very advanced.

the state of the art in person re-identification is still not very mature, with many open challenges.

the best performing re-id methods are based on the use of deep convolutional features, with the best performance achieved by using the combination of a triplet loss function and a hard example mining strategy.
the best re-identification algorithm is the one that is most appropriate for the specific application.

the performance of state-of-the-art re-id algorithms is still far from satisfactory.
there is still significant room for improvement in re-id performance, and that the current best performance of state-of-the-art algorithms is far from satisfactory.
